title: Finite projectivity over a glueing pair is detected by the two pieces of the pair
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a glueing pair (R -> R', f) and an R-module M not assumed glueable, and asserts that M is a finite projective R-module exactly when M tensor_R R' is finite projective over R' and M_f is finite projective over R_f (source lines 25777-25784). The proof establishes the non-trivial direction by assembling earlier results. Assuming the two pieces are finite projective, the proof notes it will use the finite-projective criterion without further mention, and applies the flatness criterion of the glueing pair to conclude that M is flat (proof lines 25786-25792). It then uses the faithful descent lemma for the pair to conclude that M is finite (proof lines 25793). The substantive step is the finiteness of a kernel: choosing a short exact sequence 0 -> K -> R^{oplus n} -> M -> 0, and using that a finite projective module is finitely presented while the sequence remains exact after tensoring with R' (by the Tor-vanishing property for flat maps) and with R_f, the proof concludes that K tensor_R R' and K_f are finite modules, whence K is finitely generated by the previous statement of this series (proof lines 25794-25800). Therefore M is finitely presented and hence finite projective (proof lines 25800-25801). The non-routine content is the reduction of finite projectivity of M to finite generation of a kernel, using the two-piece hypotheses.
